description.short: Beics Brenin is the mountain bike shop, hire centre, and skills school at Coed y Brenin Forest Park near Dolgellau — the UK's first dedicated MTB trail centre. Open seven days a week, it offers hardtail, full-suspension, and e-bike hire, a full retail range, bike servicing, and coaching on some of Wales's finest riding terrain.
description.shortNote: Drafted from verified facts. Editorial review needed before publishing.
description.full:
Beics Brenin — 'King's Bikes' in Welsh — sits at the heart of Coed y Brenin (King's Forest), a 9,000-acre forest park in Snowdonia National Park, owned and managed by Natural Resources Wales. Coed y Brenin is a landmark in the history of mountain biking: it was Britain's first dedicated MTB trail centre, with races first held here in 1991 and the Tarw Du (Black Bull) trail — the oldest purpose-built mountain bike trail in the UK — completed in the mid-1990s. The site now hosts eight waymarked MTB trails ranging from the gentle Green-graded Yr Afon (10.8km) to the epic 38.2km Black-graded Beast, plus a skills and practice area and, since 2024, over 100km of new gravel and adventure cycle routes accessible on hybrid or gravel bikes.

Beics Brenin operates the on-site bike shop, hire centre, and workshop as an independent business within the visitor complex. The hire fleet covers children's bikes (balance bikes through under-16 hardtails), adult hardtail MTBs (Trek), full-suspension bikes (Trek Fuel EX and Specialized Stumpjumper), and e-bikes (Trek Rail 625Wh and Specialized Turbo Levo 700Wh). All bikes are hired for use within the Coed y Brenin trail network; day hire runs 9am–4pm with a 3-hour option also available. The retail side stocks clothing and accessories from brands including Endura and Fox. Coaching, skills courses, and events are also offered.

Note: the NRW-operated visitor centre café and information counter at the same site closed permanently on 31 March 2025. The bike shop (Beics Brenin) continues to operate independently. Interior toilets are open 9:30am–4pm; exterior toilets and all trails are accessible year-round.

cover.reason: All photography on beicsbrenin.co.uk is copyright Beics Brenin 2026. The Visit Wales listing shows 7 gallery images credited to © Beics Brenin — also not freely licensed. Wikimedia Commons has some general Coed y Brenin forest trail marker images (referenced via Wikipedia article https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coed-y-Brenin), but these show trail signs rather than action/scenery and may not serve as a premium cover image. No freely licensed mountain biking photography of Coed y Brenin was confirmed with a CC-BY or CC0 licence during this research pass.
